units.why: "Specify how particular assignments relate to your course-level policy so expectations remain clear": assignment-specific clarification of rules, P04.
units.fit_note: Calls for assignment-level detail inside a course policy.

units.passage: must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor
units.policy: All use of GenAI must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor.
units.why: Both coders coded the sentence "must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor" as P04 restrict; A and B were paired at different positions in the first pass and are re-aligned here.

units.passage: Your individual instructor and the specific assignment determine the rules for using GenAI in your coursework.
units.why: "Your individual instructor and the specific assignment determine the rules for using GenAI" states who sets the rule; it is a standing principle, not a communication step (A course-start, B general). Final general.

units.passage: GenAI use may be prohibited in one course, permitted with acknowledgment in another and even required in a third.
units.why: "prohibited in one course, permitted with acknowledgment in another and even required in a third" says rules vary per course and instructor, which is P04 (A P04, B P11). The "compliance is based on the rules for that specific course" clause is P11 and is kept as its own unit (A14), because B joined two rules in one policy.

units.passage: one course may allow varying levels of permitted GenAI from one assignment to the next
units.why: "one course may allow varying levels of permitted GenAI from one assignment to the next" describes how expectations vary by assignment, a point about communicating course expectations (A course-start, B during-work). Final course-start.

units.passage: it is your responsibility to define the boundaries of acceptable GenAI use within your discipline and on a course or per-assignment basis.
units.why: Instructors are responsible for defining acceptable use 'on a course or per-assignment basis': P04.

units.passage: Faculty members have discretion to set policies for GenAI use in their courses, with transparency and alignment to learning objectives.
units.why: "Faculty members have discretion to set policies for GenAI use in their courses" delegates the decision (A neutral, B permit). Delegation is not itself a permission for AI use; neutral.

units.passage: Students are expected to understand and comply with the policies that faculty set in their courses
units.why: "Students are expected to understand and comply with the policies that faculty set" is a compliance duty for the length of the course (A course-start, B during-work). During-work.
units.fit_note: Addresses students' duty to comply, not the instructor's discretion itself. | Addressed to students: comply with instructor-set rules.

units.passage: If a blanket policy is not suitable for the course, provide clear direction in the syllabus that students should adhere to the guidelines given with each activity, assignment or assessment.
units.why: "If a blanket policy is not suitable ... provide clear direction in the syllabus that students should adhere to the guidelines" sits under "Instructor Requirements" (A must, B should). Must.

units.passage: Instructors are welcome to adapt the following to align with disciplinary use of GenAI and pedagogical practices.
units.why: 'Instructors are welcome to adapt the following' leaves final wording to each instructor and discipline, so the decision is delegated (P04); P05 already covers the templates in the previous unit.

units.passage: Each assignment will provide additional guidance as to how these tools might be part of your process and how to be transparent about the use of AI in your work.
units.why: 'Each assignment will provide additional guidance' shows the role of AI is set assignment by assignment (P04).

units.passage: However, there will be an opportunity to use AI-generated text for an extra credit assignment (not required).
units.why: 'there will be an opportunity to use AI-generated text for an extra credit assignment' is a narrow, assignment-specific exception (P04).

units.passage: AI use will be limited to one specific project, i.e. The Personal Narrative of the Other (Empathy project)
units.why: 'AI use will be limited to one specific project' (P04: allowed per assignment).

units.passage: Each assignment will provide additional guidance as to how these tools might be part of your process and how to be transparent about the use of Generative AI in your work.
units.why: 'Each assignment will provide additional guidance': P04.

units.passage: Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals.
units.why: "Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals" leaves permission to individual instructors, so P04.

units.passage: However, these tools should be used only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed by the instructor.
units.policy: Generative AI tools should be used only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed by the instructor
units.why: The text requires 'explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed'. Permission is per instructor and confined to what was allowed; P04 fits. P10 (ask when unsure) is not what is said.
units.fit_note: Adds that permission must be explicit and clear and that use is confined to the ways the instructor allows.

units.passage: Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals.
units.why: "Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals" leaves permission to individual instructors, so P04.

units.passage: However, these tools should be used only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed by the instructor.
units.policy: Generative AI tools should be used only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed by the instructor
units.why: The text requires 'explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed'. Permission is per instructor and confined to what was allowed; P04 fits. P10 (ask when unsure) is not what is said.

units.passage: OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom.
units.why: The sentence says "OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom," so the university sets no campus-wide rule and leaves the choice to instructors; that is the instructor-decides type (P04), stated as a fact.

units.passage: Instead, faculty are encouraged to make intentional, discipline-appropriate choices and to communicate those choices clearly to students.
units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to make intentional, discipline-appropriate choices', placing the decision with instructors and discipline; phrased as encouragement so modality is should.

units.passage: In addition to syllabus policy language, you are encouraged to have Generative AI policies for each assignment in your class.
units.why: Instructors are 'encouraged to have Generative AI policies for each assignment', which sets rules per assignment (P04) and asks for explicit statements.

units.passage: I will never use Generative AI to grade your work. Example Generative AI Policy: Based on the Assignment If you would like to moderate usage, meaning that Generative AI is appropriate in some instances and not in others, we encourage you to have a stand-alone Generative AI usage policy in your syllabus statement, and to also state that each assignment will have a clear Generative AI policy explaining how it may be used, or not.
units.why: Moderate usage means each assignment has its own clear AI policy; per-assignment rule (P04).

units.passage: There will be times in which you will not be permitted to use Generative AI or may only use it in particular ways.
units.why: AI permission varies: sometimes not permitted, sometimes in particular ways; the rule is set per assignment (P04).

units.passage: Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses. Those who choose not to use AI will not be required to follow these guidelines.
units.why: Principle 3 states 'Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools', delegating the decision to instructors.

units.passage: Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT.
units.why: Hybrid sample says 'Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage' GenAI, i.e. assignment-by-assignment permission (P04).

units.passage: We hope this useful resource will help you (1) understand the possibilities and the limitations of AICGTs for teaching and learning practices, content creation, assessment integrity, etc.; (2) make informed decisions about how to incorporate AI-generated content into your teaching, learning, and research activities; (3) engage your students in a reflective, responsible, productive and ethical use of these tools in various teaching and learning activities; and finally (4) help you explore and perhaps reframe your own narrative about how AICGTs will influence your professional identity as an educator and as a scholar.
units.why: The page states goals to help faculty 'make informed decisions about how to incorporate AI-generated content', delegating decisions to instructors (P04).

units.passage: Have a syllabus policy statement on what AI use is allowed, decided at your own or your unit's discretion based on the course's learning objectives.
units.policy: What AI use the syllabus statement allows is decided at the instructor's own or the unit's discretion
units.why: The same sentence says the allowed use is "decided at your own or your unit's discretion", so the university sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors or units (P04); the unit-level part is only partly captured by P04.
units.fit_note: Also lets the unit (department) decide, which P04 names only for instructors; P85 not chosen because the unit option is secondary to instructor choice. / The unit-level discretion is also named (P85).

units.passage: I join with the Office of the Provost in encouraging all faculty to consider and determine your own course philosophy and expectations around the use of generative AI tools for each of your courses, communicate those expectations in your course syllabus, and discuss them in the first week of the term.
units.policy: Faculty determine their own course philosophy and expectations around the use of generative AI tools for each course
units.why: The Dean joins the Provost "in encouraging all faculty to consider and determine your own course philosophy and expectations", leaving the AI rule to instructors (P04).
